newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: PALM OIL - Asian prices seen firm, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: PALM OIL - Asian prices seen firm, trade thin.

text.p: Asian palm oil prices are likely to stay steady to firm this week on expectations of some good demand for forwards positions, regional traders said.
Market players are awaiting official Malaysian crop figures for November for fresh leads.
The Palm Oil Registrtaion and Licensing Authority (PORLA) will release the November stock/export/output data at 0430 GMT on Monday.

"We are waiting for PORLA's numbers," a Malaysian trader said. "If the PORLA data are supportive, we may see more movements and gains in the palm market. If not, the market is likely to drift in tight ranges until year-end."
A crop report by private forecaster Ivan Wong on Friday had no impact on the market. Wong estimated output in November at 762,000 tonnes and end-November stocks at 960,000 tonnes.

"I think the third position in the Kuala Lumpur Commodity Exchange will be up 20-30 ringgit from a base of around 1,200 ringgit. There will be pretty good demand for February/March delivery," one Singapore trader in a European commodity house said. But another Singaporean dealer said that while prices may trend firm, it may be difficult to sustain the momentum.
"It's going to be quiet into the holidays and the volumes may suffer a bit," he said. "It's going to be a slow market especially towards the end of this week."
The market seems well supported near 1,200 ringgit a tonne, traders said. The February futures contract closed on Friday at 1,210 ringgit a tonne.
Indonesia palm olein prices are likely to trend steady to higher on adjustment to relatively high crude palm oil prices.
There was no margin in processing olein from crude palm oil at current prices, traders said, adding that olein prices were also expected to improve due to healthy gains in Europe.
"Local olein prices will have to adjust higher," one trader in Indonesia said. "Otherwise, players might just export crude palm oil because of the good prices there."
The trader said he expected prices to edge towards 1,450 rupiah by the end of this week.
Indonesian palm olein finished last week at 1,425-30 rupiah, up from 1,400-05 rupiah previously.
"I expect players to take fresh positions this week before the Christmas and New Year holiday season," one trader in Indonesia added.
"The indications are that olein prices will improve."
(with contributions from K.T. Arasu in Jakarta and Rene Pastor in Singapore)
